item.title: Sunday 1 PM Update, Nov 1
item.description:
The Sunday one o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for November 1, 2026: Londonderry conditions through tomorrow afternoon; a Michigan Democrat endorses the Republican for Senate two days out, and a Swedish debut win at the New York City Marathon; Iran's foreign minister calls for "rationality" as Israeli strikes kill eight in Gaza, a deadly week in Ethiopia's Oromia region, and a cyclone bearing down on India's east coast; Tesla moves Cybercab electronics into the Model 3; Anthropic's experiment in sneaking bad training data past its own monitor; Alpine Linux rebuilds its code server after an attack; your X feed; this week's Londonderry events; and a football field full of groceries in New Jersey. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Sunday 10 AM Update, Nov 1
item.description:

item.title: Sunday Morning, Nov 1
item.description:
The Sunday morning bulletin from Gumshoe News Radio for November 1, 2026: Londonderry weather with the seven-day outlook; the last weekend push before Tuesday's midterms, the FBI widens its Alaska inquiry, a deadly shooting after Birmingham's Magic City Classic, and criticism of administration Halloween posts; Trump and Netanyahu talk as the U.S. weighs renewed Iran strikes, the G20 foreign ministers part without a communique, looting in Frankfurt and a mass opposition rally in New Delhi; a look at the week ahead for markets; a court lets the NAACP's pollution suit against xAI proceed; A.I. agents join the search for alien signals and Britain expands A.I. help for planning permits; the FBI pins the Binance heist on North Korea, plus critical Linux and LXD flaws; your X feed; New Hampshire's Election Day guide; and an eight-year-old's birthday gift to strangers in Memphis. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Saturday 4 PM Update, Oct 31
item.description:
The Saturday four o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 31, 2026, Halloween: Londonderry conditions through tomorrow afternoon; a federal judge throws out the President's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal, Virginia and D.C. sue to stop the planned arch near Arlington, and a check on a viral claim about networks and a presidential address; Poland's prime minister addresses the nation and Halloween protests turn tense in Marseille; Apple passes Nvidia as the world's most valuable company and Microsoft's small computer-use model; Mistral opens the weights of its trillion-parameter model and OpenAI's new biology model for vetted researchers; an Android text message that can crash phones and a breach at Chainalysis; your X feed; a death investigation in Bow; and a bus-stop bench that made a kid jump for joy. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.
